endpoints.summary: Send the owner a notice, a question (buttons, text reply, choice, links), an HTML card or a live text panel. Prefer a native question for simple choices, normal priority and no speech. Sending isn't seeing or answering: wait with GET /v1/interactions/{id}?wait=55 (or one /v1/events loop for several)

body.name: kind
body.description: notice (one-way), question, html (a card you draw; answer comes from Bridgit.respond), pieces (a card the phone draws from pieces and sources; no HTML) or text (a live text panel you stream into with /v1/text/stream)

body.name: pieces
body.description: kind=pieces: 1-24 pieces (header, status, text, note, metrics, table, timeline, gallery, video, people, devices, draft, buttons), values as {"$source":"<source>.<path>"}. See https://bridgit.cc/learn/builder/applet-packages.md

body.name: sources
body.description: kind=pieces: up to 8 named sources: {"watch":"<your watch id>","read":"tally"|"status"} or {"call":{"path":"/v1/...","query":{}},"every_s":60-3600} (GET only)

body.name: fresh_s
body.description: kind=pieces: 30-86400; older data shows the card as stale

body.name: states
body.description: kind=pieces: your own words for the card states empty, loading, stale, paused, error

body.name: title
body.description: Up to 80 characters

body.name: text
body.description: Up to 2,000 characters

body.name: image
body.description: {"gallery_id"} or {"data_base64"}, up to 2 MB

body.name: html
body.description: kind=html: the card's HTML, up to 256 KB. Runs offline: no network, only data:image/* images; call Bridgit.respond(value) once per question view (up to 16 KB) to answer; value is a JSON string or a plain object/array, which is serialized for you. window.Bridget is the same object (the only name on 1.6.269 and older). After persistence, bridgit:answered lets the card show its confirmation; the trusted Back to questions control reloads the question for resubmission. Bridgit.act({method, path, query?, body?}) runs one of your own endpoints on the phone right away, as you, with your grants and the owner's switches, e.g. await Bridgit.act({path:'/v1/flashlight', body:{on:true, auto_off_seconds:1}}) resolves to {ok, status, body}. A request is at most 16 KB (bigger: error request_too_big, so send a capture_id or gallery_id, never photo bytes) and a JSON reply over 64 KB comes back ok: false, error reply_too_big with the fix (ask for less). You get an action.executed event for each call, so it works while you're offline. A single card can't be swiped: show progress as text ("Step 2 of 5"), not swipe or segment bars. Complete pages: GET /v1/samples. A card app that decides or watches (Jev for text, Clef for photos and sound, POST /v1/watches with the free camera change check): https://bridgit.cc/learn/decisions.md

body.name: controls
body.description: Question: 1-6 of {type: button|text|choice|link, id, label, style?, placeholder?, options?, url?, package?}. Notice: links only

body.name: priority
body.description: normal or urgent

body.name: speak
body.description: Read it aloud on the phone

body.name: no_takeover
body.description: No takeover: true delivers this interaction to the Inbox and notifications without opening it, even while Bridgit is in front. Default false: opens automatically, subject to the owner setting and Android Display over other apps permission

body.name: follow_up
body.description: Card flows: true when you will post another card once the owner answers or closes this one. The card screen says "Waiting for the next card…" and stays up to 30 s; your next card replaces it in place, and Bridgit steps back to what the owner was doing only after the last card of the flow. Post the next card as soon as the answer or dismissed event arrives; leave it out (or false) on the last card. If the owner answered from the notification without the card on screen, nothing is held and the next card opens as usual. Ignored with no_takeover

body.name: expires_in_seconds
body.description: 60 to 604800, default 86400. After it, waits return expired and you get interaction.expired, but a question stays on the owner's phone and they can still answer it late (interaction.answered with late=true)

body.name: stack
body.description: kind=html: 1-32 letters, digits, - or _. Your cards with the same stack id form one stack the owner swipes through (drag left = next, right = previous) with "n of m" and a peek of the next card; each card keeps its own id, wait and answer. Up to 10 cards per stack id; an open stack counts as one of your 5 open questions. Leave it out for a single card, which is never swipeable. Don't rely on horizontal scrolling inside a stacked card. Wait on GET /v1/events?types=interaction.answered rather than one wait per card

body.name: stack_index
body.description: kind=html with stack: position 0-9 (default: after the cards already posted)

body.name: swipe_answer
body.description: kind=html with stack: {"left": label, "right": label} (1-20 characters each). While the card waits, a swipe answers it and moves on: answer.data = {"swipe": "left"|"right", "label": ...}. Bridgit shows both labels under the card

body.name: presentation
body.description: standard (default: inside Bridgit's bordered card box, with the toolbar and the status/Dismiss strip) or full_screen (kind html only: edge to edge, system bars, toolbar and strip hidden; a tap on the screen edge or Back shows Dismiss and Exit full screen for a few seconds). A full-screen page without width=device-width in its viewport meta is scaled down to fit whole, letterboxed in black, never cropped. Compose full-screen pictures to display.viewport (or GET /v1/device/display full_screen_card; static specs are also at GET <team backend>/v1/names/{name}/specs) and show them with object-fit: contain. Other values: invalid_parameter

body.name: content_aspect
body.description: kind=html: the page's fixed shape as width:height, e.g. "16:9" or "1280x720". When it differs from the canvas by more than 10 %, the reply's display.aspect_mismatch says so (also checked from width/height in the page's viewport meta)

body.description: Instead of question: 1-10 typed questions, {id: {type: choice|noul, instructions, criteria?}}, as https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives

body.name: callback_when
body.description: With questions: the answer that calls you back, 1-5 conditions that must all hold: {answer, min?, max?} on a noul probability, or {answer, choice, min_confidence?} (default 0.8) on a choice. Jev's confidence is not the probability: 0.67 likely is about 0.34 confident

body.name: data
body.description: What to read each time (default ["location", "motion"]): location (with speed), motion (2 s accelerometer burst), steps, light, pressure, proximity, battery, device (screen, lock, headphones, network), camera (a 640 px photo; only the newest is sent to the model), sound (loud sounds: the watch runs on each loud sound instead of an interval and sends that clip to Clef; use it alone). location needs the location permission, the sensors ones the sensors permission, camera the camera permission and an unlocked phone. With only camera, window and min_readings default to 1

body.name: interval_s
body.description: Seconds between readings: 30-3600 (default 60); down to 10 only for a camera tally with local.change_check enabled. Set max_paid_per_hour to bound optional model calls. A watch keeps the phone awake and reads location each time, so pick the longest interval and expiry that work. Phone-wide limit on paid watch checks, and the account's Jev and Clef calls an hour and monthly budget: read them with GET /v1/limits (they differ per account). A still, unplugged phone may pause checks until it wakes

body.name: window
body.description: How many recent readings Jev sees, 1-20 (default 5)

body.name: min_readings
body.description: Readings to collect before the first question (default 3, at most window)

body.name: expires_in_s
body.description: Stop after this long, up to 86400 (default 7200). With a tally: up to 7776000 (90 days, default 30 days)

body.name: repeat
body.description: false (default): one callback, then the watch ends. true: keep watching, at most one callback per cooldown_s

body.name: cooldown_s
body.description: With repeat: seconds between callbacks (default 600)

body.name: callback_url
body.description: Where to POST the result, as well as your registered callback and /v1/events. Same rules as callbacks: a tailnet address, or https on the internet if the owner allows internet callbacks. Signed with the callback_secret in the reply

body.name: context
body.description: Anything Jev should know, up to 2000 characters ("the owner commutes by bike")

body.name: label
body.description: A short name for logs and lists (default: the question)

body.name: model
body.description: Who answers, and whether you pay: clef (Cloudflare Clef-omni, paid; the default with camera, about $0.000105 a photo), jev (TypeSafe, paid; the default without camera, about $0.000065 a photo, $0.000008 for text), glm (GLM 5.3 Flash through OpenRouter, paid), or none (local only, free: needs camera, takes no question, and calls you back when the picture changes). Paid models share the phone's hourly limit

body.name: camera
body.description: With camera in data: rear (default), front or an enrolled lan:<id> (needs lan_camera access)

body.name: additional_cameras
body.description: Up to seven other enrolled camera ids or phone lenses. The watch rotates one per reading under its shared hourly cap; each source keeps its own change history. Excludes people watches.

body.name: local
body.description: With camera in data: the free change check on the phone before any paid call. {change_check: true (default; false = pay for every photo), sensitivity: low | normal (default) | high (high notices smaller changes, so pays more often), learn_noise: true (default; when a paid call for a change gave the same answer, ignore those spots for 10 min), max_reuse_s: 30-3600 (default 300; ask again after this long even if nothing changed)}. A reused answer can still call you back (answered_locally: true). It looks at the photo only: other data you read doesn't make it pay

body.name: people
body.description: With model none and camera in data: when the picture changes, take a short burst of photos, find faces on the phone, crop them (and embed them with an on-phone face model once it has downloaded) and hand them to the applet's private web portal. {burst: 1-5 (default 3; the changed photo counts), burst_gap_ms: 300-3000 (default 800), battery_floor: 0-100 (default 50; only while charging or at least this full), max_bursts_per_hour: 1-60 (default 20), min_face_share: 0.005-0.5 (default 0.01; smaller faces are ignored)}. Crops stay in memory only (at most 48, 6 hours). Needs repeat: true. Only in an installed applet's own plan with the people_seen permission the owner approved (refused here and from card actions), and it captures only while that applet's web portal is on with photo sharing

body.name: sound
body.description: With data ["sound"]: {sensitivity: quiet | normal (default) | loud (how much louder than the room's quiet level a sound must be), reuse_s: 0-1800 (default 300; a loud sound this soon after the last paid check that sounds like it, compared on the phone by its frequency fingerprint, reuses that answer for free (answered_locally, similarity in last_check); a different-sounding one is checked; 0 = ask every time)}. No interval_s: the phone's loudness check wakes the watch, at most once every 30 s. Model must be clef. Paid checks default to 6 an hour; set max_paid_per_hour to change it. Needs the sounds permission and switch and the microphone permission. The watch shows listening true/false and not_listening_reason

body.name: start_paused
body.description: Create the watch paused until resumed. Default false. A paused watch takes no readings and fires no rules.

body.name: max_paid_per_hour
body.description: At most this many paid model calls an hour for this watch, 1-240 (default: only the phone-wide limit). Checks over it are skipped, not paid. Also lowers what the watch takes from the phone-wide limit

body.name: tally
body.description: Count on the phone, for weeks, with you offline ("how many times did the dog eat today"). {track: the question id to count (default: your only question; with question, "match"), labels?: the choice options to count (default all), min_confidence?: 0-1 for a choice (default 0.5), min?: 0-1 for a noul, which counts as its own id when that likely (default 0.5), seen?: one condition, e.g. {answer: "dog_present", min: 0.6}; readings count, and add to watched time, only while it holds, gap_s?: readings this far apart are one episode (default 3 x interval_s, at least 60), label_gap_s?: map tracked labels to individual episode gaps in seconds (1-21600); coverage still uses gap_s, min_episode_readings?: drop shorter episodes (default 1), keep_days?: 1-30 (default 30)}. callback_when becomes optional (with it, callbacks come at most once per cooldown_s, and the watch never ends on a match). Read it with GET /v1/watches/{id}/tally; a card reads it with Bridgit.act, on a button or a timer of 5 minutes or more (each call is an action.executed event, and events keep only your newest 1,000)

body.name: rules
body.description: With tally: up to 5 rules the phone checks after every reading. {id, when, do?, cooldown_s?}. when: {none_for_s, of, while_seen?: true} (no episode of that label for so long; while_seen counts only watched time), {fewer_than, of, by: "10:00"} (fewer episodes today by that local time; once a day), or {at_least, of, within_s}. A rule that fires sends you a watch.rule event {watch_id, rule, message, today, action} and runs do, exactly one of: {"flow":"<workflow id>", "with"?: {…}} starts one of your called or button workflows (its steps read the rule as {"$trigger":"message"}, "of", "today", "rule", "watch_id"; action is {flow, status: started|dropped|flow_not_active|flow_not_found|bad_with, run_id}); {"step":{"type":"notice","title":"No meal seen yet","text":{"$trigger":"message"},"priority"?:"urgent"}} or {"step":{"type":"speak","text":…}} runs one step from the workflow menu (needs interactions or speaker); or one of your own endpoint calls {method, path, body?, query?}, as a card's Bridgit.act would ({message} and {label} in its text are filled in). cooldown_s: default the rule's own time span
